A1.justification: Both readable 19-page PDFs describe the same work and support comparison of their text, equations, tables and figures. Neither includes an appendix or the referenced supplementary material; unseen supplementary experiments cannot be compared.

before.justification: v1 reports original node and triplet retrieval experiments on extended SceneFun3D and FunGraph3D annotations, quantitative ablations in Tables 1–3, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark experiments, quantitative ablations and qualitative results in Tables 1–3 and Figure 4.

M1.justification: The 2D relationship anchoring, multi-cue node association, temporal graph optimization and global hierarchy shaping procedures are unchanged. Added explanations of Equation 1 symbols clarify existing quantities without changing the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same extended SceneFun3D and FunGraph3D coverage, including hierarchical relationships and tabletop objects. Annotation counts and the stated robotic manipulation demonstration setting remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain FunGraph, OpenFunGraph, OpenFunGraph Tabletop and OpenFunGraph Hierarchy in the same comparisons. Newly cited related work is not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation scope narrows: v2 removes the statement about supplementary results under the original OpenFunGraph protocol and no longer asserts quantitative evaluation of robotic-arm demonstrations. The retained retrieval thresholds, Hungarian matching, GPT-5 control and keyframe downsampling are unchanged. These deletions do not establish that the unavailable supplementary experiments changed.

E4.justification: The supplied analyses retain the same Assoc-OpenFG, No-GO-Count and 2D-Hierarchy ablations, their findings, and Figure 4 qualitative examples. The ablation introduction is clarified without adding or revising an analysis.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the experimental results.

E6.justification: v2 removes the 17:13 runtime comparison with OpenFunGraph on FunGraph3D from Section 6.1, while retaining the qualitative runtime-comparability assertion. All values in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged, including the proposed method's FunGraph3D overall node and triplet scores of 60.2 and 55.6.

T1.justification: The graph formulation, constraints and Equations 1–9 are unchanged. The added explanations of accumulated point clouds, projected boxes and appearance histograms restate existing mathematical meanings.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark-expansion contribution, proposed pipeline and performance claims. The stated node and triplet retrieval advantages remain 13.9% and 20.5%.

C2.justification: The explanations of retrieval gains and ablation behavior are retained. Both versions state the same limitations concerning extreme occlusion, restricted viewpoints and dependence on detection, segmentation and VLM quality.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository link in the abstract, providing access information absent from v1. Repository contents and availability cannot be verified from the PDFs; implementation settings otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion distinguishing open-vocabulary part segmentation from temporally fused functional entities and graph relationships. Three references are added: Going Denser with Open-Vocabulary Part Segmentation, OV-Parts, and Reconstructing Functional 3D Scenes from Egocentric Interaction Videos.

P1.justification: v2 corrects scattered spelling and grammar errors, clarifies Equation 1 notation, updates author affiliations and correspondence information, replaces the placeholder running title, and adds acknowledgements. The main section order and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Existing Figures 1, 3 and 4 are enlarged, Figure 1 moves to the top of its page, and Table 1 moves alongside Tables 2–3 on page 13. Content reflows across pages, but no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity and usability through notation explanations, better related-work positioning, larger figures, editorial corrections and a stated code-access link. The scientific method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged. Removing the numerical runtime comparison weakens efficiency reporting, but the overall gains remain limited and positive.
